I am using Python 3.13 and Pygame 2.6.1 for an alligator game.

Write a small example where the player alligator is a pygame.sprite.Sprite and automatically detects when it collides with a prey sprite by using a built-in on_collision() method from the Pygame Sprite class.

When the collision happens, print "Prey caught!" and remove the prey sprite.

Use only built-in Pygame sprite features.

 def make_baby_gator(direction, scale):
     """Build the shape-drawn alligator and rotate/scale it for its growth stage."""
     # Drawing in a separate transparent surface keeps the body-part coordinates
     # simple; the completed image can then face whichever way the player moved.
     gator = pygame.Surface((180, 120), pygame.SRCALPHA)

             dark_green,

         pygame.draw.polygon(gator, dark_green, leg_points)
         pygame.draw.polygon(
             gator,
             gator_green,
             [(x + 2, y + toe_direction * 2) for x, y in leg_points],
         )
         toe_x, toe_y = leg_points[2]
         pygame.draw.line(
             gator,
             belly_green,
             (toe_x, toe_y),
             (toe_x - 5, toe_y + toe_direction * 5),

             gator,
             belly_green,
             (toe_x + 5, toe_y),
             (toe_x + 1, toe_y + toe_direction * 6),
             2,
         )
 
     # A raised, wide head narrows into the long, squared alligator snout.
     pygame.draw.ellipse(gator, dark_green, (96, 31, 43, 58))
     pygame.draw.ellipse(gator, gator_green, (100, 34, 38, 52))
     pygame.draw.polygon(

     # Two visible eyes, nostrils, and a jaw line give the head reptile features.

     angle = -direction.as_polar()[1]

 import pygame
 
 
 pygame.init()
 screen = pygame.display.set_mode((640, 480))
 clock = pygame.time.Clock()
 
 
 class Gator(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
     def __init__(self):
         super().__init__()
         self.image = pygame.Surface((60, 40))
         self.image.fill((40, 170, 70))
         self.rect = self.image.get_rect(center=(320, 240))
 
     def update(self, keys):
         speed = 4
         self.rect.x += (keys[pygame.K_RIGHT] - keys[pygame.K_LEFT]) * speed
         self.rect.y += (keys[pygame.K_DOWN] - keys[pygame.K_UP]) * speed
 
 
 class Prey(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
     def __init__(self, position):
         super().__init__()
         self.image = pygame.Surface((30, 30))
         self.image.fill((230, 190, 50))
         self.rect = self.image.get_rect(center=position)
 
 
 gator = Gator()
 player_group = pygame.sprite.GroupSingle(gator)
 prey_group = pygame.sprite.Group(
     Prey((120, 100)),
     Prey((500, 140)),
     Prey((450, 360)),
 )
 
 running = True
 while running:
     for event in pygame.event.get():
         if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
             running = False
 
     player_group.update(pygame.key.get_pressed())
 
     # Uses sprite rects for collision and removes each caught prey from its groups.
     for prey in pygame.sprite.spritecollide(gator, prey_group, dokill=True):
         print("Prey caught!")
 
     screen.fill((30, 90, 60))
     player_group.draw(screen)
     prey_group.draw(screen)
     pygame.display.flip()
     clock.tick(60)
 
 pygame.quit()
